Erected in 2004 in preparation for the millennium anniversary of Thăng Long, the statue celebrates the enlightened monarch who played a pivotal role in the country's history.

The statue depicts King Lý Thái Tổ standing gallantly, his right hand firmly grasping the scroll of the historic Chiếu dời đô edict, which he issued in 1010. According to legend, upon arriving at the site of what would become Hanoi, Lý Thái Tổ witnessed a golden dragon ascending from the Red River, prompting him to rename the city Đại La to Thăng Long, marking the beginning of a new era of prosperity and glory for the nation.
